page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance featuring 4 vCPUs backed by 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The server is allocated 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It operates on the KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU core allocation. CPU cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set availability includes AVX-512 variants (f, vnni, bf16) and hardware cryptography flags including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, contains no attached local storage, and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation shows strong performance in single-core CPU tasks, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3073.57 placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core operations land within average ranges, indicated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6150.83 and a PassMark CPU score of 7545.19. Compression tasks demonstrate mixed results: single-threaded gzip compression reaches 28.95 GB/sec (average tier), while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores 26.39 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25%. Storage- and memory-bound transactional operations display lower relative efficiency, with PassMark database operations recording 2068.79, Redis SET performance yielding 5.7 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measuring 5.45 GB/sec.

The ecs.g8a.xlarge instance provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for tasks that benefit from high single-core execution speed without requiring local high-speed storage devices. Because local storage is absent, deployment scenarios require network block storage. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, lightweight web application backends, and single-thread bound processing tasks, while high-concurrency database services or disk-bound IOPS pipelines will encounter performance limitations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor at 2.7 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of memory and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Built on an x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, it includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and hardware AES instruction sets. The server lacks local storage and GPU hardware. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU throughput in the top 25% range, while overall multi-core execution remains average. Memory-heavy database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and Redis SET throughput test in lower performance bands. Offering a balanced memory ratio without local disk overhead, ecs.g8a.xlarge delivers efficient processing for general-purpose application workloads, single-threaded computing, and standard web application backends.
